archetypes.name: oos-pipeline
archetypes.rationale: Cross-script OOS producer, serializer, tally, and disposition changes can regress only on end-to-end review-core flows.
archetypes.prompt_body: Trace accepted out-of-scope findings from tally-code-votes through emit-tally, review-and-fix, accepted sink files, counters, and filing gates. Look for mismatched assumptions about header formats, OOS_ACCEPTED_COUNT, aliasing output paths, missing oos.md behavior, and multi-round accumulation. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: shell-portability
archetypes.rationale: The diff adds shell helpers and rewrites shell parsing where Bash 3.2 and BSD portability are explicit constraints.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the new and changed shell scripts for Bash 3.2 compatibility, BSD awk/sed portability, quoting, temp-file cleanup, trap behavior, and safe handling of empty or multiline blocks. Pay special attention to normalize-oos-block-header.sh, oos-serialize.sh, emit-tally.sh, tally-code-votes.sh, and review-and-fix.sh. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: parser-parity
archetypes.rationale: The same OOS and security-routing semantics are implemented in awk, Bash/Python regexes, and docs, creating parity risk.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the OOS header and security-tag recognition rules across python/oos.py, oos-non-security-block-count.awk, lib-vote-tally.sh, oos-serialize.sh, tests, and documentation. Check for semantic drift around tagged legacy FINDING headers, bare FINDING headers, fenced or backtick-wrapped tokens, heading tags, and focus-area fields. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: holdback-routing
archetypes.rationale: Security OOS holdback behavior changed and failures could publicly file sensitive findings or suppress legitimate public OOS items.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate whether security-tagged out-of-scope blocks are consistently held locally and never written to public accepted-OOS sinks or issue-filing paths. Also check for false positives that hold ordinary public OOS items because of incidental security wording, markdown examples, body headings, or inline formatting. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: regression-harness
archetypes.rationale: The plan relies heavily on new targeted harnesses to catch subtle production-only OOS drops and overwrite paths.
archetypes.prompt_body: Assess whether the added or changed tests actually exercise the production failure modes described in the plan, including emit-tally preserve versus serialize/truncate, dual-sink aliasing, skipped-routing normalization, legacy-header counters, and Python/Bash parity. Look for tests that pass without validating the intended invariant or miss important negative cases. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
